title: Dedicated: autoscaling burst controls, utilization reporting, and throughput guarantees
author: Priya Singh
commits: add: introduce burst_budget and sustained_throughput fields to Dedicated pool config
fix: enforce burst accounting in autoscaler decision loop and add backpressure signal
chore: wire utilization telemetry and add dashboards + docs
description: Motivation: Dedicated customer fleets occasionally see short-term spikes that exceed committed sustained throughput but are still within acceptable burst envelopes. Current autoscaler treats short spikes as sustained demand which causes unnecessary capacity churn and missed SLAs for other customers. This PR introduces burst budget controls, explicit sustained_throughput guarantees, and fleet-level utilization reporting so operators can understand headroom and enforce fair usage. Summary of changes: 1) config: add 'burst_budget' (tokens/min) and 'sustained_throughput' (tokens/sec) to Dedicated pool spec with validation and defaults; 2) autoscaler: update decision loop to account for burst budget consumption and to emit a backpressure signal when burst budget is exhausted; autoscaler now computes two scaling targets (sustained_target and burst_target) and prefers sustained_target for long-term actions while honoring burst_target for short windows; 3) telemetry: add utilization_collector that aggregates per-GPU token/sec, KV cache hit ratios, and burst budget usage; expose kafka metrics and a Grafana dashboard JSON; 4) rollout: add a rollout policy that enables burst controls behind a feature flag and performs canary on 5% of fleets; 5) migration: include a migration script that populates default sustained_throughput for existing pools based on recent 30d p95 throughput; 6) docs: dedicated-autoscale.md and release notes describing new knobs and recommended values. Testing and validation: unit tests for budget accounting and scaler logic (tests/test_autoscale.py), integration canary run on staging (dedicated-canary-3) with traffic replayed which showed reduced scale-up churn and improved 99th pct latency for neighboring fleets, load test harness run with synthetic bursts to validate budget depletion behavior. CI: full test-suite and linters passed after re-running flaky integration test once (reason: timing-sensitive test). Rollout plan: merge to main, enable feature flag by default for new fleets, gradual migration for existing fleets using migrate_burst_configs.py with a 7-day monitor window and automatic rollback if utilization regressions exceed thresholds. Observability: new grafana dashboard 'Dedicated Fleet Utilization' and alerts for burst_budget_exhausted and sustained_throughput_violation. Backwards compatibility: default values make the feature opt-out; no breaking behavior expected for existing customers. See linked Linear tickets ENG-4321 and SRE-104 for follow-ups on autoscaler tuning and alert thresholds. Merge: squash-merged to main on 2026-02-21 after approvals and green CI.

release_notes: Added burst_budget and sustained_throughput controls for Dedicated pools. Autoscaler now respects burst envelopes to reduce unnecessary scale churn. New util dashboard and alerts. Migration tool provided to backfill sustained_throughput for existing pools.
